extracted.intended_audience: AI researchers, incident reporters, policymakers, and practitioners documenting AI harms
extracted.subtask_description: Documenting and classifying a specific AI incident (here, Microsoft’s Tay chatbot) using the AI Incident Database fields and taxonomies; includes metadata, taxonomy labels, and harm/risk characterizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates which, if any, of the following types of AI failure describe the incident: "Specification," i.e. the system's behavior did not align with the true intentions of its designer, operator, etc; "Robustness," i.e. the system operated unsafely because of features or changes in its environment, or in the inputs the system received; "Assurance," i.e. the system could not be adequately monitored or controlled during operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select one or more of Specification, Robustness, Assurance to characterize the failure mode. The page lists all three as applicable for Tay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical System
rubrics_metrics.description: Where relevant, indicates whether the AI system(s) was embedded into or tightly associated with specific types of hardware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values distinguish hardware-embedded systems from software-only deployments. Example on the page: "Software only."

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of Autonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which the AI system(s) functions independently from human intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines High (no human involved in action execution), Medium (system generates a decision and a human oversees resulting action), Low (system provides decision-support and a human makes/executes the decision). The page assigns "Medium" to Tay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of End User
rubrics_metrics.description: "Expert" if users with special training or technical expertise were the ones meant to benefit from the AI system(s)’ operation; "Amateur" if the AI systems were primarily meant to benefit the general public or untrained users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to indicate intended audience sophistication. Tay is classified as for "Amateur" users (general public).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Sector Deployment
rubrics_metrics.description: "Yes" if the AI system(s) involved in the accident were being used by the public sector or for the administration of public goods ... "No" if the system(s) were being used in the private sector or for commercial purposes ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary flag with examples: public-sector (e.g., public transportation) vs private/commercial. Tay is marked "No."

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief description of the data that the AI system(s) used or were trained on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise description of inputs/training data. Example given for Tay: "Twitter users' input."

rubrics_metrics.name: Entities (implicated and harmed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify which entity is presented as the main cause of the risk and who was harmed. Example text: "Alleged: Microsoft and Taybot developed and deployed an AI system, which harmed Twitter Users."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record both alleged responsible parties and categories of harmed entities (e.g., organization names, user groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applied Taxonomies
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists which taxonomies were applied to classify the incident (e.g., CSETv0, CSETv1, GMF, MIT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the taxonomy labels used for the entry so users know the classification scheme and provenance of labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Metadata (ID, Report Count, Date, Editors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured metadata used to index and track the incident: Incident ID, Report Count, Incident Date, Editors, and Citation Info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these fields for identification, versioning, and provenance. On the page: Incident ID = 6; Report Count = 28; Incident Date = 2016-03-24; Editors listed (Sean McGregor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Interest Intangible Harm
rubrics_metrics.description: An assessment of whether a special interest intangible harm occurred. This assessment does not consider the context of the intangible harm, if an AI was involved, or if there is characterizable class or subgroup of harmed entities. It is only asking if a special interest intangible harm occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary/qualitative assessment separate from contextual analysis. Page marks this field as "yes" for Tay and includes a note: "4.6 - Tay's tweets included racist and misogynist content, far-right ideology, and harmful content against certain religions, etc."

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of Incident (Year/Month/Day)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fields capturing the date of the incident with instructions: Enter in the format of YYYY (year), MM (month), DD (day).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple harms, list earliest; if precise date unavailable, estimate or leave blank. For Tay the page lists 2016 / 03 / 23.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Domain and Risk Subdomain (MIT Taxonomy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk Subdomain: a finer-grained classification (example: "1.2. Exposure to toxic content"); Risk Domain: the higher-level domain taxonomy of AI Risks (e.g., Discrimination & toxicity, Privacy & security, Misinformation, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Domain to capture broad category (the page assigns "Discrimination and Toxicity") and Subdomain for precise hazard (here exposure to toxic content).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity (Cause), Timing (Stage), Intent (Expected vs Unexpected)
rubrics_metrics.description: MIT taxonomy fields: Entity — which entity is presented as the main cause of the risk (page value: "Human"); Timing — stage in the AI lifecycle at which the risk occurred (page value: "Post-deployment"); Intent — whether the risk is presented as occurring as an expected or unexpected outcome from pursuing a goal (page value: "Intentional").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record causal actor (human/system), lifecycle stage (design, training, deployment, post-deployment), and whether harm was an expected/intentional outcome or unintended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variants and Similar Incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: A "variant" is an AI incident similar to a known case—it has the same causes, harms, and AI system. Instead of listing it separately, we group it under the first reported incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use variants to avoid duplicate entries; note that variants do not need external reports. The page provides a 'Seen something similar? Submit a Variant' prompt and shows similar incidents by textual similarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Reports / Sources (Timeline and Citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: A list/timeline of external media and source reports relevant to the incident (e.g., news articles, blog posts, press coverage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include source metadata and links to support the incident entry; the page lists numerous contemporaneous news articles and blog posts (BBC, Guardian, Verge, Wired, etc.) and provides expand/collapse and 'Read More' links for each.
